pass_a_gloss: For what reason is the silence of the many, and to me most of all now, and both willingly and unwillingly, I am being forced to be silent and to hold my tongue. For I have neglected, in a certain way, the good and fine words, which are spoken and composed by the chosen and approved men, with names and verbs, in a certain order, without hindrance. But I, being less capable of this charming task, have not been able to accomplish it, which is truly a Greek work. But now, for eight years, I have not been able to write or speak anything, either great or small, nor have I heard anyone else writing or speaking privately, or providing public display-speeches and contest-speeches, except for those wonderful men who have mastered beautiful philosophy, to whom elegance and refinement of names are of less concern. But, putting their voices in second place, they wish to examine and proclaim the things themselves, with precision and accuracy, not because they do not want to, but because they want to very much, the good and precise things of the thoughts, and to express them in speech. But perhaps they are not able to do so, because they have the sacred and divine word, and the word that is in the expressions, which is easy to understand, and they want to encompass the soul of each individual, which is difficult and human. For if one is to think and find something, silence is a friend and helper. But the one who is eloquent, you will not find anywhere else, except in voices and the continuous practice of them. And the mind is seized by another kind of learning, and the mouth is bound by the tongue, if I were to try to say something, even small, in the Greek voice, our wonderful men, who now direct the affairs of all men under the human rule, not being hindered or learning effortlessly, being themselves accurate and refined and wonderful, and being called most Greek, having been expressed and handed down in the Roman voice, which is impressive and boastful and conforming to the royal authority, but burdensome to me. But since our words are like images of the passions of our soul, to those who are able to speak, like good painters, with technique and with the material of colors, not only similar but also varied and beautiful, to write and express the writings, without being hindered in any way, we would agree.

pass_b_english: What is the reason for the silence of the many, and for me most of all now, and both willingly and unwillingly I am being forced to hold my tongue and to be silent. For I have neglected, in a certain way, the good and fine words which are spoken and composed by the chosen and approved men, with names and verbs, in a certain order, without hindrance. But I, being less capable by nature of this charming task, have not been able to accomplish what is truly a Greek work. Yet now an eight-year period has already passed for me, during which I have not been able either to speak or to write anything at all, great or small, nor have I heard anyone else writing or speaking privately, or providing public display-speeches and contest-speeches, except for those wonderful men who have mastered beautiful philosophy, to whom elegance and refinement of names are of less concern. But, putting their voices in second place, they wish to examine and proclaim the things themselves as each is, with precision and to express them, not because they do not want to, I think, but because they want to very much, the good and precise things of the thoughts, and to form them in speech with grace and good expression. But perhaps they are not able to do so, because they have the sacred and divine word, and the word that is in the expressions, which is easy to understand, and they want to encompass in one and the same soul, which is small and human, the capacities of two men, each of which are the most opposite things. For if one is to think and find something, silence is a friend and helper in some way. But the one who is eloquent, you will not find anywhere else, except in voices and the continuous practice of them. And the mind is seized by another kind of learning in a terrible way, and the mouth binds the tongue, if I were to try to say something, even something small, in the Greek voice. Our wonderful men, who now direct the affairs of all men under the human rule, not being hindered nor learning effortlessly, being themselves accurate and refined and wonderful, and being called most Greek in a word, having been expressed and handed down in the Roman voice, which is impressive and boastful and conforming to the royal authority, but burdensome to me. But it would not have been otherwise possible, nor would it have been desirable for me, to become twofold at any time. But since our words are nothing other than certain images of the passions of our soul, to those who are able to speak, like good painters, with technique, and most technical at that, and with the material of colors, not only similar but also varied and most beautiful, to write and express the writings with the mixed multitude of flowers, without being hindered in any way, we would agree.
